memory_update.text: USAR should be stored as the reference rare-earth mine-to-magnet name for this node, not necessarily the most underfollowed asset.
UUUU is a strong underfollowed processor/qualification candidate because its rare-earth oxide exposure is masked by uranium categorization.
CODI is a hidden-exposure candidate through Arnold Magnetic Technologies; later layers must verify materiality of Arnold to consolidated CODI economics.
MTRN is a specialty-materials hypothesis for defense/aerospace requalification bottlenecks; requires program-level or customer qualification evidence before promotion.

For specialty materials and requalification-dependent inputs, the likely chokepoint is not just mining capacity but qualified non-Chinese or domestic processing, metals/alloys, magnet manufacturing, QA/QC validation, and defense customer acceptance.

Need a later pass on SEC filings and contract databases for sole-source/qualified-supplier language across beryllium, specialty titanium/nickel alloys, SmCo/NdFeB magnets, coatings, and rare-earth oxide-to-metal conversion.

summary: Expanded the US-listed universe for policy-driven specialty materials and requalification-dependent inputs. The strongest underfollowed lane appears to be downstream processing, magnet qualification, specialty alloy/beryllium materials, and hidden magnet-system assets rather than only mines. Key chokepoint logic: defense/aerospace programs may not be able to switch sources quickly because materials must satisfy DFARS, purity, QA/QC, customer validation, and program qualification requirements.
